answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line is at 94% with no buffer, so deferral or a primary switch would raise delivery risk. Incumbent already refused a mid-cycle price reopen, but this is a renewal window: c4 says benchmarking at renewal moved price and terms, and c6 says a longer commitment unlocked volume pricing without cutting scope. Renewing as-is (c1) protects continuity but does not meet the 18% spend cut. c5 deferral was for a non-critical month-to-month case and does not apply. Verifying c4 (negotiation actually recovered margin at renewal) and c2 (whether a low-cost primary switch was truly low-risk/fast enough) before committing.
